acceptance: READ FIRST: this task's acceptance list (85 items) and verify list (45 commands) are longer than the run prompt shows (wan-implement fences acceptance at 3000 and verify at 2000 characters). pieces.piece_layout(shapes, w, bounds=None) cuts every tensor along dim 0 on multiples of Q_t = lcm(row length, 128) elements (row length = numel/shape[0]; 1 for 1-D), equal by default (piece sizes differ by at most one quantum), w == 1 gives one piece, a tensor with fewer quanta than peers gets empty pieces; explicit bounds that are not monotone, not aligned or do not tile [0, numel) raise ValueError naming the tensor.

pieces.exchange_units(chunk) lists units in forward order: the Embed's tables (tok, pos) one unit first; each SplitLinear module one unit (weight and bias); each block's other trainable tensors one unit; the Head's norm in the Head linear's unit; every trainable parameter in exactly one unit; a tied parameter (tie_embeddings: Head.out.weight is Embed.tok.weight) is in the Embed's unit only (BA-42); deterministic.

The piece fold starts from an fp32 copy of microbatch 0's widened piece and adds in index order; on real toy-GPT gradients (fp32, bf16 and fp16 autocast, w 1..8) every piece equals the matching slice of the whole-tensor OrderedAccumulator result bitwise; controls that must differ: a bf16 clone as the start value, a zeros start with a -0.0 input.
Piece-local cast to bf16 and fp16 equals the slice of the whole-tensor cast for every one of the 2^32 fp32 bit patterns (exhaustive, chunked; NaN payloads compared bitwise).

Piece-local AdamW (the reference's constructor: lr, betas (0.9, 0.95), eps 1e-8, weight_decay 0) over 3 steps equals slices of whole-tensor AdamW in params, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq and step at w 1..8, with ragged explicit bounds and a tensor with fewer quanta than peers, and also when the step is applied unit by unit (only that unit's grads set).
No kernel draws from the torch RNG (torch.get_rng_state() is unchanged across every call).
pieces.consumer_dtype is removed with its test: the working-copy dtype has one source, wgrad.gather_dtypes (MODEL-I7, interface I-2), which stage-pieces uses.

JobSpec gains wire ('fp32' default | 'native'), shard ('zero1' default | 'pieces', job-wide), emission_order (per stage 'store' default | 'forward'), piece_bounds (None or explicit per-stage per-parameter bounds), pacing ('link' default | 'shared') with peer_egress_mbps and peer_ingress_mbps [stage][peer], sites [stage][peer] and uplink_mbps per site pair and direction; to_json/from_json round-trips them exactly and a spec JSON without them loads with the defaults.

This is the frozen finalize contract of interface I-7, which scheduler-pieces-plan's planner satisfies in the same wave: finalize accepts every combination I-7 lists as planner output (shard 'pieces' with wire 'native' and stream_grads True; wire 'native' with stream_grads True; piece_bounds None, or keyed by the stage chunk's named_parameters() name, the same '<layer index in chunk>.<param name>' names exchange_units uses, with bounds on multiples of pieces.quantum(shape)); a test 'spec_m2b_planner_contract' builds one spec per I-7 planner combination and finalizes it. A change to this contract is a recorded spec conflict naming scheduler-pieces-plan, never made.
recipe_digest is identical for two specs that differ only in these fields (the oracle cache is not split).
BA-53: two specs that differ only in the M2b fields have equal pins() and equal recipe_digest; pins() is otherwise unchanged (the M2 RUNTIME-I15 tests pass).

exchange.NeedFirstQueue (interface I-5): one per (sender, destination); pop returns the item with the smallest key (fwd_unit, kind, step, mb, seq), kind 0 for a gather (PARAMS) and 1 for a gradient (GRADS); LOSS frames and the shutdown sentinel sort after every exchange item; push and pop are thread-safe and pop blocks with a timeout. Unit tests with randomized pushes from several threads, named 'need_first'.

exchange.chunk_object(unit, payload) splits one unit's frame payload into self-contained chunks of at most 16 MiB carrying (unit, offset, length) in the OBJ envelope, with no frame header change (BA-40); reassembly by (type, step, mb, sender, unit) never mixes two units of one microbatch (BA-13); unit tests named 'need_first' or 'chunk'.

exchange.check_frame(kind, env, tensors, expect) is the receiver's boundary validator: every malformed GRADS or PARAMS frame (dtype not in the plan's table, shape not the slice or piece, mb outside [0, M), step neither current nor next, repeated (step, mb, unit, sender), unknown unit) raises FrameError naming its class; one unit test per class named 'frame_check'. Cost per frame: one dict lookup and a few integer comparisons (no tensor op).

exchange.CopyEngine (interface I-5): submit(fn) runs every exchange D2H/H2D copy on the engine's own thread and returns a future; on CPU a unit test proves the caller's thread never runs the copy (thread identity), named 'copy_engine'; the CUDA copy-stream path (pinned chunks of at most 16 MiB, events) is built and labelled real-hardware pending (F7).

exchange.HoldCounters (interface I-5): monotonic per-step counters of host gradient pieces held or queued, gathers queued out and received awaiting H2D, and own pieces on the device awaiting their prefix; per-step maxima (end_step) rendered as one 'WT_HOLD' line by line(step); no tensor op, device sync or RNG draw; unit tests named 'holds'.

logical_ckpt (interface I-6): build_manifest(step, width, peer, layout, tensors) records (name, offset, length, sha256 per 16 MiB chunk) plus the step, the wave's width, the slot's peer index and the full layout; select_wave(read_manifest, peers_present) takes w_old and the layout from slot p0's manifest and returns exactly p0..p(w_old-1), refusing, naming the slot, one whose manifest names another width, layout or step, or another peer index than its own; peers_present lists every peer index of the stage with a wave at the resume step, and one >= w_old whose manifest names that step and width w_old is an extra index, refused naming it (RUNTIME-I12); one >= w_old naming another width belongs to an older wave and is never read as state (BA-51).

logical_ckpt.assemble(payloads) rebuilds the logical master, m, v and step counters per tensor in canonical name order, merges the loss histories of every slot, and takes the RNG and non-trainable state every slot holds; it refuses, naming it, before any state is applied: pieces that leave a gap or overlap, a chunk sha256 mismatch, a missing manifest, a manifest step different from the payload's, a missing peer, two values for one (step, mb), a missing (step, mb) on the final stage, and slots whose RNG or non-trainable state differ (one unit test each).
